result.summary: Enables the `-Wextra-semi` compiler warning flag in CMakeLists.txt and removes redundant semicolons across dozens of header and source files. It also adjusts the fallback definition of `TRACEPOINT_SEMAPHORE` in `src/util/trace.h` to expand to a forward declaration struct so that trailing semicolons at call sites remain valid.
result.problem: Redundant semicolons throughout the codebase produce unnecessary syntax noise and prevent enabling compiler diagnostics that catch accidental extra semicolons.
evidence: PR description: "Enable -Wextra-semi and delete all the redundant semicolons. Waiting on a pull of the libmultiprocess subtree."
result.scope_notes: The PR spans 66 files but is almost entirely mechanical semicolon removals. It includes a `[nomerge]` commit with fixes to `src/ipc/libmultiprocess` that waits on an upstream subtree sync before merging.
result.changed_since_previous: No substantial changes to the approach or commit structure; the PR has been rebased while still carrying temporary libmultiprocess subtree fixups.
result.card: Enables the -Wextra-semi compiler warning flag in CMake and strips redundant semicolons across 66 files in the codebase. It improves compiler hygiene and prevents redundant semicolons from being introduced in the future. Importance is low as it is an internal cosmetic cleanup, and the PR currently includes a nomerge commit waiting on a libmultiprocess subtree update.

risk.why: The diff consists almost purely of removing redundant semicolons, which carries negligible risk of behavioral regression.
